title: Compact policy state and lightweight regional failover adapter refactor
creator: Sana Rao
description:
Problem:
The current routing policy runtime mixes in-memory global locks, per-request mutation, and region-specific heuristics. This creates contention under bursty workloads, makes fallbacks hard to reason about, and complicates regional pruning logic. We've seen transient P95 latency spikes on the smart-router hot path during incident INC-2025-11-03 which traced back to policy state reconciliation.

Goal:
1) Replace the mutable global policy state with a compact, append-only snapshot store that can be read lock-free on the request hotpath.
2) Introduce a lightweight regional failover adapter abstraction so region-specific fallback logic is pluggable, testable, and can be hot-swapped without touching the hotpath.
3) Remove a set of legacy heuristics that duplicate capacity/affinity calculations and unify metrics emitted for fallback decisions.

Success criteria:
- Hotpath router CPU utilization reduced by >= 15% on staging for the same QPS.
- End-to-end P95 latency for route selection reduced by >= 10% in canary.
- No meaningful increase in error-rate or incorrect fallback choices in daily traffic tests.
- New metrics: policy_snapshot_version, snapshot_apply_latency, failover_adapter_invoke_ms, regional_prune_count are emitted and visible in Console.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change higher-level routing policy grammar or customer-facing policy config. Separate follow-up will expose adapter tuning knobs to the Console.

Design summary:
- Snapshot store: a compact immutable representation produced by the control plane whenever policy or capacity metadata changes. Snapshots are versioned (monotonically increasing) and published into a small in-memory ring buffer on each router node. The hotpath reads the latest snapshot pointer with an atomic load; no locks during evaluation.
- Delta apply: background reconciler applies incremental diffs so snapshot generation is cheap and fast.
- Regional failover adapter: define an interface with two responsibilities: (a) compute candidate fallback targets given a snapshot and request context, (b) emit structured decision metadata used by observability. Provide a default adapter (current logic ported) and a pruning adapter (simpler, faster heuristics) to validate trade-offs.
- Migration: dual-run option where the new adapter runs in parallel (shadow mode) producing decision traces; after validation we flip traffic.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Spike (2w): prototype snapshot ring buffer and atomic read pattern; microbenchmarks vs current code.
2) Implement snapshot generation in control plane and delta apply (3w).
3) Implement adapter interface + port existing fallback logic into default adapter (2w).
4) Add pruning adapter and opt-in canary (1w).
5) Integrate metrics and Console dashboards, add tracing hooks and decision traces (1w).
6) Canary rollout (2w) and broader rollout with gradual % ramp and alerting.

Rollout and testing:
- Start with internal staging traffic (100% staging). Run A/B with shadow mode for 3 days measuring decision parity.
- Canary 1 (5% prod): monitor P50/P95/P99 route-selection latencies and decision parity.
- Canary 2 (25% prod): enable pruning adapter for opt-in customers only.
- Full rollout after 2 weeks of stable canaries.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- Add metrics: policy_snapshot_version (gauge), snapshot_apply_latency_ms (histogram), failover_adapter_invoke_ms (histogram), regional_prune_count (counter).
- Add structured logs for fallback decisions (sampled) with fields: snapshot_version, adapter_kind, reason_code, chosen_target, candidate_list_len.
- Build a Console dashboard: Routing -> Policy snapshots, Failover latency, Decision parity.

Risk and mitigations:
- Incorrect fallbacks due to logic porting: mitigation -> extended shadow run and decision parity checks, automated rollback hooks.
- Snapshot staleness after control plane outage: mitigation -> fallback to last-known-good snapshot and conservative adapter behavior (increase retry/backoff).
- Memory pressure on router nodes: mitigation -> compact binary encoding and cap ring buffer to N snapshots.

Stakeholders:
- Owner: Maya Chen (routing infra)
- Reviewer: Diego Alvarez (serving runtime), Priya Patel (SRE), Alex Novak (Product)
updates: 2025-11-12: Spike complete. Prototype snapshot ring buffer shows 22% lower median lock time in microbenchmarks. Code in branch feature/eng-32177-snapshot-spike.

2025-12-02: Control plane delta apply prototype merged to staging branch (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/178). Need follow-up to harden error handling when diffs fail validation.

2026-01-15: Adapter interface spec reviewed with Diego and Priya. Agreed on structured decision log schema. Added two adapter implementations: default (ported) and prune-fast (experimental). PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4127 opened.

2026-02-05: Canary tests in staging passed parity checks for 72 hours. Observed 16% CPU reduction on router hotpath at target QPS. Minor mismatch cases (0.08% of requests) traced to edge cache TTL differences; patching control plane TTL propagation.
2026-02-28: Security review not required for this change; infra config change will require separate ops runbook. Preparing canary in prod (5%).
2026-03-03: Canaries at 5% for 48 hours — P95 route selection decreased 12%. Decision parity 99.93%. Ready for 25% ramp pending SRE signoff (Priya).
notes: Follow-ups: expose adapter selection flag in Console, add e2e tests covering cross-region failovers, write runbook for snapshot rollback and emergency flip-to-default-adapter.
